Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

DMAR 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-15

Breaking Changes in 1.1.0

DMAR 1.1.0 names the total sample size, the number of predictors, a planner’s planning value, and the desired width one way, and names an argument for the quantity it holds rather than for a symbol. The DMAR 1.0.x names listed here are not accepted: a call that gives one stops with R’s “unused argument” error. The exceptions, all of them, are listed under Old Names That R Still Matches, after the table. There is no deprecation period and no function that maps an old name to a new one. Change the call. Three functions are removed, with no alias; the call that replaces each is given under One Function for Each ANOVA Effect Size.

The Count in the Partial and Semipartial Correlation Functions Changed Meaning

var_partial_r(), var_semipartial_r(), expected_partial_r(), ss_aipe_partial_r(), ss_aipe_semipartial_r(), ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity(), and ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity() took J, the number of variables partialed out. They take p, the total number of predictors in the regression of Y on X and the variables partialed out, in the place J held, and p = J + 1. A DMAR 1.0.x call that gave the count by position still runs, and now describes one fewer variable partialed out. var_partial_r(.3, 100, 2) was a partial correlation given two other variables and is now a partial correlation given one; ss_aipe_partial_r(.3, 2, .2) planned for two variables partialed out and now plans for one. Add 1 to the count in every such call: var_partial_r(.3, 100, 3), ss_aipe_partial_r(.3, 3, .2). A call that named the count (J = 2) stops with “unused argument” and becomes p = 3. p must be a whole number of at least 2; with nothing partialed out the correlation is the simple correlation, which var_r(), expected_r(), ss_aipe_r(), and ss_aipe_r_sensitivity() cover.

One Function for Each ANOVA Effect Size

  • eta_squared_partial(), omega_squared_partial(), and ci_eta_squared_partial() are removed. eta_squared(), omega_squared(), ci_eta_squared(), and ci_omega_squared() take estimand = c("all", "total", "partial") and report the total and the partial value of each effect in columns of their own (see Total and Partial Eta Squared and Omega Squared). There is no alias. Replace

    DMAR 1.0.x call DMAR 1.1.0 call
    eta_squared_partial(fit) eta_squared(fit, estimand = "partial")
    eta_squared_partial(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = ) eta_squared(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = ) (the partial value; estimand = "partial" leaves out the NA total column)
    omega_squared_partial(fit) omega_squared(fit, estimand = "partial")
    omega_squared_partial(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = ) omega_squared(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = , estimand = "partial")
    ci_eta_squared_partial(fit) ci_eta_squared(fit, estimand = "partial")
    ci_eta_squared_partial(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = ) ci_eta_squared(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = , estimand = "partial")

  • The columns of the four tables are named for the estimand. A script that read $eta_squared, $omega_squared, $ci_lower, or $ci_upper from these tables reads the new name. The values under the old names were the partial values, and the new argument does not change them.

    function DMAR 1.0.x column DMAR 1.1.0 column
    eta_squared() eta_squared eta_squared_partial
    omega_squared() omega_squared omega_squared_partial
    ci_eta_squared() eta_squared, ci_lower, ci_upper eta_squared_partial, eta_squared_partial_ci_lower, eta_squared_partial_ci_upper
    ci_omega_squared() omega_squared, ci_lower, ci_upper omega_squared_partial, omega_squared_partial_ci_lower, omega_squared_partial_ci_upper

    With estimand = "all", the default, the columns of the total (eta_squared_total, omega_squared_total, and for the intervals eta_squared_total_ci_lower and so on) come before those of the partial value; estimand = "partial" gives the table of 1.0.x with the new names. The effect, stratum, F_value, df_effect, df_error, and N columns are unchanged.

  • estimand is the second argument of eta_squared(), omega_squared(), ci_eta_squared(), and ci_omega_squared(), after object. A call that gave F_value by position (as the second argument) stops; name it.

  • tidy() of these tables gives one row per effect and estimand, the rows of the total before those of the partial value, with term naming the estimand ("eta_squared_total", "eta_squared_partial") where it named "eta_squared". glance() of a table with more than one row of tidy() gives the estimands in term, separated by a comma.

Renamed Arguments

An argument is named for the quantity it holds and for the role of the value. A population value that a planner or a sensitivity function takes begins with true_, as do those of the analysis of variance, analysis of covariance, and regression data generators; the value a sensitivity function plans the design from begins with supposed_ (estimated_ or est_ in DMAR 1.0.x, which suggested an estimate from data, where the value is a planning assumption); and a null value begins with null_. The quantity is named in words: a correlation is cor (true_cor, true_cor_YX, cor_lower), a contrast contrast and a standardized one std_contrast, a regression coefficient reg_coef and a standardized one std_reg_coef, a squared multiple correlation R2, a mean mean, a standard deviation sd (true_sd, and true_sd_X and true_sd_Y when the variable is named), a population variance true_var_ followed by what it is the variance of (true_var_within, true_var_error, true_var_trend), a covariance matrix cov_matrix, a factor loading factor_loading, and a residual variance residual_var. A function that computes the same quantity from population values or from estimates (cohen_f(), ci_srsnr(), covmat_from_cfa(), var_ete(), var_indirect_effect()) names its arguments without a role. A sample size given so that the power or the precision at that size is returned is specified_N (the total, or the one group) or specified_n_per_group. The table gives the name each argument had in DMAR 1.0.x.

simulate_ancova_data() mu_y, mu_x, sigma_y, sigma_x, rho, n true_mean_Y, true_mean_X, true_sd_Y, true_sd_X, true_cor, n_per_group
simulate_ancova_factorial_data() mu_y, mu_x, sigma_y, sigma_x, rho_y_x, rho_x_x, n true_mean_Y, true_mean_X, true_sd_Y, true_sd_X, true_cor_YX, true_cor_XX, n_per_cell
simulate_regression_data() rho_YX, rho_XX, mu_Y, mu_X, sigma_Y, sigma_X true_cor_YX, true_cor_XX, true_mean_Y, true_mean_X, true_sd_Y, true_sd_X
simulate_longitudinal_polynomial(), simulate_longitudinal_logistic(), simulate_longitudinal_gompertz(), simulate_longitudinal_negative_exponential(), simulate_longitudinal_richards() n, occasions n_per_group, n_occasions

Old Names That R Still Matches

R matches an argument name by its leading characters, and a function that passes ... to another program does not refuse a name itself. The table lists 602 old names, a name counted once for each function that had it. Of these, 536 stop with “unused argument”. These 66 do not:

  • The same quantity under its new name; the call runs as before. w = in ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity() and design_consequences() (matched to width); df_res = in ss_power_sem() (df_restricted); n = in ci_c(), ci_c_ancova(), ci_sc_ancova(), equivalence_c(), cohen_f(), is_orthogonal_set(), variance_components_mls(), simulate_anova_data(), simulate_ancova_data(), ss_seq_c(), mr_smd(), and power_equivalence_c() (matched to n_per_group, the per-group size it always was; in the five power planners that took n and take specified_n_per_group, ss_power_c(), ss_power_sc(), ss_power_c_ancova(), ss_power_split_plot_anova(), and ss_power_composite_ancova_2group(), n = now stops with “unused argument”); and n = in power_equivalence_md(), power_density_equivalence_md(), and power_equivalence_md_plot() (matched to n_per_treatment, the same quantity, now that the degrees of freedom are df_error and no other argument begins with n: a 1.0.x call that gave the degrees of freedom by position runs, and one that named nu stops for nu). Write the full name: the match is R’s, it is not a name these functions have, and it ends the day one of them gains another argument that begins with the same letters.
  • Another argument; the call stops, with a message about something else. es = in the six ss_aipe_crd_es_*() functions is matched to es_type when es_type is left out, and the call stops where the effect size is needed, with a message about es_type or about the missing effect size; a fixed-budget call that does not ask for the expected width never used the effect size and still runs. a = in ss_power_indirect_effect() is matched to alpha_level, so a 1.0.x call stops for the unused b. n = in ecvi() is matched to npar when npar is left out, and the call stops for the missing multiplier; a call that also names npar stops with “unused argument”. f = in ss_power_factorial_anova() and ss_power_factorial_ancova() is matched to factor_levels when the levels are given by position, and the call stops because a value of Cohen’s f is not a vector of levels; a call that names factor_levels stops with “unused argument”.
  • More than one argument; the call stops. w = in ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity(), and ss_aipe_src_sensitivity() stops with “argument matches multiple formal arguments” (which_predictor, width), as does n = in ci_c_ancova_bp() (n_per_group, n_covariates), in the five simulate_longitudinal_*() functions (n_per_group, n_occasions), in ci_sc() (n_per_group, ncp), and in simulate_ancova_factorial_data() (n_per_cell, n_covariates). d = in ss_power_mixed_effects() stops with the same message when desired_power and directional are both left out; when one of them is named, d is matched to the other and the call stops for the missing true_smd.
  • Another argument, or ...; the function reads the name and stops. n = in var_icc() would be matched to n_raters, and in var_alpha() to n_items, so a call that named only the sample size and gave the count by position, var_alpha(.80, n = 100, 10) or var_icc(.60, n = 30, 4), would run with the two values exchanged: 100 items and 10 respondents, or 30 raters and 4 subjects. n = in bayes_one_sample_t() would be matched to null_mean, so a call that named the sample size n would take it as the comparison value for the mean. The three functions read the names in the call and refuse n with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid that says to write N =. A 1.0.x call of var_icc() or var_alpha() that named every argument also named k or p_items (and rho in var_icc()) and stops with “unused argument”; n = in bayes_paired_t(), which has no argument that begins with n, stops with “unused argument” too. Four names would reach a ...: t_value = in ci_nc_t(), which was a second name for ncp, would pass to the root finder; mu_0 = in ci_mahalanobis() would reach the root search of ci_nc_F(); psi = in ci_sc() would reach ci_nc_t() and stop inside its root finder; and psi = in ci_c_ancova() would be dropped without a word under procedure = "t" and passed to ci_c_ancova_bp() under "bryant_paulson". Each function refuses the name with the same class and says to write ncp =, null_mean =, or contrast =.
  • Given to a function that passes ... to lavaan, beside the new arguments; the function reads the name and stops. Sigma =, pop_model =, mu =, desired_width =, and N = in ss_aipe_composite_sem(); Sigma =, pop_model =, mu =, and N = in ss_power_composite_sem(); Sigma = and N = in ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity(); Sigma = and desired_width = in ss_aipe_sem_path(); and est_Sigma =, true_Sigma =, desired_width =, and N = in ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity() (true_Sigma was that function’s 1.0.x name for the generating matrix, now true_cov_matrix). Each of the five functions checks the names in ... against the arguments and options of lavaan before anything is fitted, and a name that is neither is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid that gives the name as it was typed and points to the function’s Renamed arguments section.
  • Given to a function that takes ... for its root search; the call stops, but not with “unused argument”. chi_square = in ci_nc_chisq() goes to ..., and the call stops at once because chisq is missing (class dmar_argument_invalid). sigma_squared = in ci_srsnr() with means stops the same way because var_within is missing; with F_value, it reaches the noncentral F search, which stops with “unused argument (sigma_squared = …)” inside a condition of class dmar_computation_failed.

ci_cv(), ss_aipe_c(), ss_aipe_cv(), ss_aipe_R2(), ss_aipe_sc(), ss_aipe_sc_ancova(), ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_sm(), and ss_power_R2() took ... and used it for nothing, so a name they did not have was dropped without a word and the call ran on the default of the argument that was meant: ss_power_R2(true_R2 = .3, p = 3, N = 50) planned for the default power and returned 36. They no longer take ..., and any name they do not have, old or misspelled, is an “unused argument”. The two counts of the simulation that ss_aipe_R2(verify_ss = TRUE) runs, which were read from ... as g and G, are the arguments G_initial (the replications for each candidate N of the coarse search) and G (the replications of the final pass); g and G differed only in case. ci_c_ancova_bp() and the three Bryant-Paulson distribution functions took a ... they did not use and no longer take it, for the same reason: ci_c_ancova_bp(num_covariates = 2) would otherwise have been computed for the default of one covariate without a word. So did ci_c(), ci_reg_coef(), plot_randomization_test(), and R2_mixed_effects(), and ci_rc() and ci_src(), which passed theirs to ci_reg_coef(), where nothing read it; none of the six takes ... now. No exported function is left with a ... that its body does not use. covmat_from_cfa() read only tol_det from its ..., so a misspelled name, or a third value given by position, was dropped without a word; tol_det is now an argument of its own, after factor_loading and residual_var, and the function takes no ....

In ss_power_r() the name N is gone and no other argument took it: ss_power_r(true_cor = .3, N = 50) stops, and the call is ss_power_r(true_cor = .3, specified_N = 50). The null value was rho_0 and is null_cor, as the other null values are null_R2 and null_rmsea; the 1.0.x planning value rho then matches nothing and stops.

ss_aipe_c() takes the error variance one way, as true_var_error, the name in ss_aipe_c_sensitivity() and ss_power_contrast(). MSwithin was a second name for it and SD was its square root; both are gone, with the three checks that the values agreed, so a 1.0.x call that gave SD = s gives true_var_error = s^2. A population contrast is true_contrast in every planner and an observed one contrast; the standardized contrast is true_std_contrast, where the two standardized contrast sensitivity functions called it true_psi, the 1.0.x name of the unstandardized contrast elsewhere.

In the planners for the analysis of variance, Cohen’s f is a planning value and is true_f, beside true_eta_squared and true_eta_squared_partial, in ss_power_one_way_anova(), ss_power_rm_anova(), ss_power_split_plot_anova(), ss_power_factorial_anova(), and ss_power_factorial_ancova(); the row of ss_power_contrast() that holds the f of the contrast is true_f too (effect_size_f). Cohen’s f squared is true_f2 in ss_power_R2(), ss_power_R2_change(), ss_power_reg_coef(), and ss_power_rc(), the argument and the row. The correlation among the repeated measures and the sphericity value of ss_power_rm_anova() and ss_power_split_plot_anova() are true_cor and true_epsilon, and the proportion of within-cell variance the covariates explain in ss_power_factorial_ancova() is true_covariate_R2. The five planners report the noncentrality parameter in the row noncentral_f_parm, the name in ss_power_R2(), and the degrees of freedom in df_effect and df_error, the names in ss_aipe_omega_squared() and ci_eta_squared(). The number of subjects of ss_power_rm_anova(), each measured on every occasion, is the total sample size, so it is specified_N when given and the row necessary_N when planned.

cohen_f(), ci_srsnr(), and covmat_from_cfa() are calculators, not planners: each computes the same quantity from population values or from sample summaries and estimates, so their arguments carry plain quantity names without true_. cohen_f() takes means, var_within, n_per_group, eta_squared, sd_means, and sd_within (mu, sigma_squared, n, sigma_m, sigma); given population values it returns the population f, and given sample summaries it returns the plug-in value from the same calculation, which is not an unbiased estimate of f. ci_srsnr() takes the observed group means, var_within (the pooled within-group mean square; sigma_squared), and n_per_group as an alternative to F_value; with population values in their place, the interval is a hypothetical one, not an interval from observed data and not the expected interval of a planned study. covmat_from_cfa() takes the factor loadings and residual variances, population values or estimates from a fitted model, as factor_loading and residual_var (lambda, psi_squared), and returns its matrix as the element model_implied_cov (population_cov): the matrix is unchanged, and the new name says what it is whether the loadings and residual variances are population values or estimates. covmat_from_cfa(lambda = l, psi_squared = p)$population_cov is covmat_from_cfa(factor_loading = l, residual_var = p)$model_implied_cov.

The planners for composite power in the analysis of variance and covariance (ss_power_composite_anova(), ss_power_composite_factorial_anova(), ss_power_composite_ancova(), ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova(), ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het(), and ss_power_composite_ancova_2group()) name their population values as the single-effect planners do: true_means, true_sd, true_cor (the covariate correlations, correlations), true_covariate_R2, and true_sd_X, the standard deviation of the covariate (sd_cov), which is the name the two ANCOVA contrast sensitivity functions give the same quantity. The fields of each element of effects are renamed too: Cohen’s f is true_f and partial eta squared is true_eta_squared_partial (f, partial_eta_squared), so list(factors = 1, f = 0.25) becomes list(factors = 1, true_f = 0.25). A field is not an argument and R does not check it, so the planners now do: an element of effects with a field they do not read is refused (see Calls That Are Now Refused). The rows follow: true_f_<label>, noncentral_f_parm_<label>, and df_error, the names the single-effect planners use. The total sample size beside the per-cell or per-group answer is the row total_N in both branches, the rule for an implied total everywhere else in the package (it was necessary_N beside a planned size and specified_N beside a size that was given); when the correlations differ in absolute value and the size was planned, it is approximate_total_N beside approximate_n_per_cell or approximate_n_per_group (approximate_N). The attributes the plot() method reads from the tables of ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het() and of ss_power_composite_ancova(slopes = "heterogeneous") (means, correlations, sigma, sd_cov) are renamed with the arguments: true_means, true_cor, true_sd, and true_sd_X. ss_power_c_ancova() takes true_sd and specified_n_per_group (sigma, n), as ss_power_c() does.

A size per group is n_per_group and a size per cell is n_per_cell, in the estimators as in the planners: ci_c(), ci_sc(), ci_c_ancova(), ci_sc_ancova(), equivalence_c(), cohen_f(), is_orthogonal_set(), variance_components_mls(), ss_seq_c(), mr_smd(), simulate_anova_data(), and simulate_ancova_data() took n and take n_per_group (one number for equal groups, or one per group where the function allowed it); ss_power_c(), ss_power_sc(), and ss_power_split_plot_anova(), where the size is given so that the power at that size is returned, took n and take specified_n_per_group; simulate_ancova_factorial_data() takes n_per_cell. ci_c() and ci_sc() had n and N, a per-group size and the total, apart only by the case of one letter. In power_equivalence_md(), power_density_equivalence_md(), and power_equivalence_md_plot() the size is n_per_treatment: the number of subjects who receive each treatment, which is the size of each group in a parallel design and every subject in a crossover, the n of the standard error sigma * sqrt(2 / n) in both. The three functions take the equivalence bounds as lower_bound and upper_bound, the true difference or ratio as true_effect, and the error degrees of freedom as df_error (ltheta1, ltheta2, and ldiff in power_equivalence_md(), theta1, theta2, and diff in the other two, and nu in all three). The grid attached to the plot keeps its column labels (n=24); its first column, diff, is true_effect. power_equivalence_c() takes n_per_group for independent groups; the number of units of a paired design, new in this release, is N (see Equivalence and Noninferiority of a Contrast).

The contrast planners name their population values as the sensitivity functions do. The error standard deviation is true_sd in ss_power_c(), ss_power_equivalence_c(), and power_equivalence_c() (sigma), as in ss_seq_c_sensitivity(); ss_power_contrast() takes true_means and true_var_error (mu, sigma_squared); ss_aipe_sc_ancova() takes true_sd_anova, true_sd_ancova, and true_sd_ratio (ratio alone is an allocation ratio elsewhere); and the values the two ANCOVA contrast sensitivity functions generate their data from are true_mean_Y, true_sd_Y, true_mean_X, and true_sd_X. The data generators for the analysis of variance and covariance and for regression name their population values the same way: simulate_anova_data() takes true_mean and true_sd (mu, sigma); simulate_ancova_data() takes true_mean_Y, true_mean_X, true_sd_Y, true_sd_X, and true_cor (mu_y, mu_x, sigma_y, sigma_x, rho), and simulate_ancova_factorial_data() the same with true_cor_YX and true_cor_XX (rho_y_x, rho_x_x); and simulate_regression_data() takes true_cor_YX, true_cor_XX, true_mean_Y, true_mean_X, true_sd_Y, and true_sd_X (rho_YX, rho_XX, mu_Y, mu_X, sigma_Y, sigma_X). mr_smd() and mr_cv() keep the symbols of the published procedure (A, epsilon, gamma, m0); their rows now name the sizes they hold: n_1 and n_2 and pilot_n_per_group in mr_smd(), N and pilot_N in mr_cv(). var_omega_squared() takes the value its formula is evaluated at as true_omega_squared (population_omega_squared), the name in ss_aipe_omega_squared(). In the six ss_aipe_crd_es_*() functions write true_es =, and in ss_power_mixed_effects() true_smd =; what R does with es = and d = is under Old Names That R Still Matches.

ss_power_pcm() and ss_aipe_pcm() give the variance of the individuals’ change coefficients and the level one error variance the same names, true_var_trend and true_var_error (tau and level_1_variance in ss_power_pcm(), variance_trend and error_variance in ss_aipe_pcm()), and ss_aipe_pcm_sensitivity() plans from supposed_var_trend and supposed_var_error. ss_aipe_pcm() takes the sampling-error variance of one individual’s estimated change coefficient (Kelley & Rausch, 2011, Equation 19) as true_var_trend_error (variance_true_minus_estimated_trend), and ss_power_pcm() reports the same quantity in the row of that name (error_var_of_slopes). ss_power_pcm() took the group difference in the change coefficient as beta and a flag, standardized, that said whether beta was divided by the between-subject standard deviation of the change coefficient. It takes the difference under the name of its scale: true_std_reg_coef for the standardized difference (beta under the 1.0.x default) and true_reg_coef for the difference in the units of the change coefficient (beta with standardized = FALSE). Exactly one is given; both or neither is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid. ss_power_pcm(beta = -.4, tau = .003, level_1_variance = .0262, frequency = 1, duration = 4, N = 238) is ss_power_pcm(true_std_reg_coef = -.4, true_var_trend = .003, true_var_error = .0262, frequency = 1, duration = 4, specified_n_per_group = 119). The two come first among the arguments, so a 1.0.x call that gave beta, tau, and level_1_variance by position gives both and is refused rather than read on the other scale. The table reports the difference on both scales, in the rows true_reg_coef and true_std_reg_coef (unstd_coefficient, std_coefficient), whichever was given, and the power is unchanged. The help of ss_power_pcm() keeps the symbols of Raudenbush and Liu (2001) in its formulas and says which argument each one is.

In the planners for an indirect effect each path is a standardized regression coefficient of the population the plan is made for, so the paths are true_std_reg_coef_a, true_std_reg_coef_b, and true_std_reg_coef_direct, and the product of the two paths is the row true_std_indirect_effect. The power of the indirect effect in ss_power_indirect_effect() is the row power_ab (actual_power), followed by power_a and power_b, and tidy() and glance() read it as the power of the design. var_indirect_effect() computes the same variances from population values or from estimates, raw or standardized, so its arguments carry neither true_ nor std_; mediate() keeps its rows a and b, which are estimates.

In the planners for structural equation models a population covariance matrix is true_cov_matrix and the matrix a sensitivity study is planned from is supposed_cov_matrix; the rows of ss_power_composite_sem() that echo the population value of each parameter are true_<label>, as in ss_aipe_composite_sem(). In ss_power_sem() df and df_full keep their names.

In the functions for one sample and for paired data, the size of the one sample, the number of pairs, and the number of trials are each the total sample size, so bayes_one_sample_t(), bayes_paired_t(), ci_proportion(), and ci_eigenvalue() take N; a call that gave the size by position (ci_proportion(17, 50)) is unchanged. The eigenvalue that ci_eigenvalue() brackets was chosen with k and is chosen with which_eigenvalue, as which_predictor and which_path choose theirs. The per-group sizes of bayes_independent_t(), ci_ratio_of_means(), and design_consequences() keep n_1 and n_2. In ss_aipe_cliff_delta() ratio keeps its name (the allocation ratio is a constant of the design, not a planning value).

A null value is null_ followed by the quantity. bayes_one_sample_t() and ci_mahalanobis() take the comparison value of the mean as null_mean (mu_0), and welch_t() and summary_t_test() take the null value of the difference between the means as null_mean_diff (mu), beside null_cor in ss_power_r(), null_R2 in ss_power_R2(), and null_rmsea in ss_power_sem().

The proportion of intervals no wider than the desired width is the row pct_ci_less_width in every sensitivity function and in design_consequences() (pct_ci_less_w; every other name in the package spells the width out), and the rows of ss_aipe_composite_sem() that hold the same proportion for each parameter are pct_ci_less_width_<label> (width_within_desired_<label>).

A count is n_<things>. The number of groups is n_groups in cv_tukey_hsd(), cv_bryant_paulson(), and the three Bryant-Paulson distribution functions (groups, num_groups), and the number of random covariates is n_covariates there and in ci_c_ancova_bp() (covariates, num_covariates); covariates in ancova() and mediate() names columns and keeps its name. The per-group size of ci_c_ancova_bp() is n_per_group. The number of random permutations of procrustes_phi() is n_resamples, the name in randomization_test(), randomization_test_paired(), and vargha_delaney_A(). The five simulate_longitudinal_*() functions take n_per_group, the number of units in each population (one number, or one per population; never a total), and n_occasions, the number of measurement occasions per unit. In ecvi() the divisor is multiplier: it is the multiplier with which the chi square was formed from the fit function, the total sample size under the normal likelihood and the total less the number of groups under the Wishart likelihood, so n named it for one case only.

The number of items is n_items, the number of raters n_raters, the number of clusters n_clusters, and the number of level one units in a cluster cluster_size, in every function that takes or reports one. ss_aipe_reliability() and ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity() took the number of items as i and var_alpha() as p_items; the row of reliability(), reliability_alpha(), reliability_omega(), reliability_omega_categorical(), and reliability_kr20() that holds it was J and is n_items, the name glance() already gave it, and the row of ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity() was items. ss_aipe_icc(), ss_aipe_icc_sensitivity(), and var_icc() took the number of raters as k; the help keeps k in the formulas and in the names of the forms ("ICC(1,k)"). ss_power_mixed_effects() took n, rho, and J and takes cluster_size, true_icc, and specified_n_clusters_per_arm: the number of clusters in each arm, not the total n_clusters, so its rows are necessary_n_clusters_per_arm and specified_n_clusters_per_arm, and its noncentrality parameter is in the row noncentral_t_parm, as in ss_power_c() and ss_power_smd(). cluster_size has no default and is checked first.

An intraclass correlation that a planner takes as a planning value is true_icc: in ss_aipe_icc() (rho) and ss_aipe_icc_sensitivity() (true_rho; a correlation is true_cor everywhere else, and the value the sensitivity study is planned from is supposed_icc, which was estimated_rho), in ss_power_mixed_effects() (rho), in the twelve ss_aipe_crd_*() functions (icc_Y), and in ss_aipe_mixed_effects() (icc). var_icc() takes the intraclass correlation its variance is evaluated at as icc, as in design_effect().

The total variance of the outcome in a two-level plan is true_total_var: in ss_aipe_mixed_effects() (sigma2_y) and ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity() (true_sigma2_y, with supposed_total_var for estimated_sigma2_y), and in the ss_aipe_crd_*() functions (total_var), where true_var_within is the within-cluster variance alone. Two names that differed by one capital no longer hold two quantities. The sensitivity function also plans from supposed_var_X and supposed_icc (estimated_sigma2_x, estimated_icc) and takes the population slope as true_reg_coef (true_beta), whose simulated summaries are the rows mean_reg_coef, median_reg_coef, and sd_reg_coef.

The twelve planners for a cluster randomized design name every population value with true_: true_var_between, true_var_within, true_total_var, true_icc, true_R2_between, and true_R2_within, and in the six for the standardized effect size true_icc_covariate (icc_Z) beside true_es. The number of covariates beside the treatment indicator is n_covariates (num_predictors; the value is unchanged, and the total number of predictors is p = n_covariates + 1). The number of individuals in a cluster is the argument cluster_size of the four functions that take it (n_individuals); the functions that solve for it report it in the row necessary_cluster_size, beside necessary_n_clusters in the two that solve for both, and a size that was given is not repeated in the table. The function names keep n_individuals. The four functions that plan from a width echo it in the row width, as the other AIPE planners do, and the width column of tidy() and glance() is that desired width for every AIPE planner (NA for a plan made from a budget and for a planner that does not echo the request); the expected or assured width is the glance() column of that name. The number of processes of the six ss_aipe_crd_es_*() functions is ncpus (multicore, num_proc), the name in the bootstrap functions. The two costs are cluster_cost and individual_cost, and the number of simulated data sets of the six ss_aipe_crd_es_*() functions is G, as in every other function that simulates (nrep). The row that reports the width no longer carries the effect or the assurance in its name: it is expected_width without an assurance and assured_width with one, and the assurance is in a row of its own, assurance. In 1.0.x the row was, for example, width_of_unstd_conditions_diff_with_0.8_assurance, a name that changed with the value asked for.

ss_aipe_reliability() names its population as a planner does: true_cov_matrix (S, which is a sample covariance matrix in the estimators), true_factor_loading (lambda), true_residual_var (psi_square), and true_item_covariance (cor_est: the help defines it as the common covariance of every pair of items, which is their correlation only for standardized items, and it is a planning value, not an estimate). The replications of the two stages of its assurance search are G_initial and G (initial_iter, final_iter), the names in ss_aipe_R2(), and an assurance plan reports the rows assurance, assurance_attained, and G (specified_assurance, empirical_assurance, final_iter), the names in ss_aipe_partial_r() and ss_aipe_semipartial_r(). The estimators (reliability_alpha() and the rest) keep S, data, and items. The reliability ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity() plans from is supposed_reliability (estimated_reliability): a planning assumption, not an estimate from data.

The measurement model and item response functions name their parameters for what they are (see the table). irt_information() reports the grid in the column trait_value and carries the attributes discrimination, threshold, and trait_value_max_information; the columns a and b of an irt_grm() table keep their names, and the help of irt_grm() and irt_information() says what they are. A call of irt_information() that gives the values by position is unaffected.

Every population value a planner for a regression coefficient takes carries true_ and is named for its quantity: the coefficient is true_reg_coef_j in the units of the data and true_std_reg_coef_j when it is standardized (DMAR 1.0.x used b_j for the first and beta_j for both), a squared multiple correlation is true_R2_ followed by its variables, and the standard deviations and correlations are true_sd_Y, true_sd_X, true_cor_XX, and true_cor_YX. The estimators name what they are given the same way, without true_ (reg_coef_j, se_reg_coef_j, sd_Y, sd_X, std_reg_coef_j).

The regression coefficient sensitivity functions lost standardize: the name of the function says the scale. ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity(), and ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity() report the unstandardized coefficient, as their 1.0.x default did, and ss_aipe_src_sensitivity() reports the standardized one, as its 1.0.x default did. A call that gave standardize stops with “unused argument”. The default of noncentral is TRUE in ss_aipe_src_sensitivity() and FALSE in the other two, as in DMAR 1.0.x, so the call that replaces ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity(standardize = TRUE) or ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity(standardize = TRUE) is ss_aipe_src_sensitivity(noncentral = FALSE), and the call that replaces ss_aipe_src_sensitivity(standardize = FALSE, noncentral = FALSE) is ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity(). ss_aipe_src_sensitivity(standardize = FALSE), with its default noncentral = TRUE, becomes ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity(noncentral = TRUE), which is refused when the sample size is planned from supposed variances that are not 1 (see Calls That Are Now Refused). With standardize = TRUE, ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity() gave the same power (the t statistic does not depend on the scale), so such a call drops the argument.

One name has one meaning, and the bounds of an equivalence region are named for the quantity they bound: smd_lower and smd_upper, contrast_lower and contrast_upper, cor_lower and cor_upper, and prop_diff_lower and prop_diff_upper in equivalence_proportion_paired(), which is new; plot_equivalence(), which draws whatever estimates it is given, takes effect_lower and effect_upper. cles(), nnt_from_smd(), and proportion_of_superiority() used smd_lower and smd_upper for confidence limits on d, as arguments and as rows; those are now smd_ci_lower and smd_ci_upper, the names DMAR gives the limits of an interval named for its estimate, so cles(smd = .5, smd_lower = .2, smd_upper = .8) stops with “unused argument”. convert_delta_lambda() takes smd, and convert_lambda_delta() and convert_lambda_R2() take ncp; the function names keep their symbols.

Renamed Output Rows and Columns

A row or column that echoes a renamed argument is renamed with it, a row that summarizes simulated estimates is named for the quantity (mean_reg_coef_j, mean_contrast, mean_std_contrast), and the columns of the per-replication files that the sensitivity functions write with filename follow the rows they summarize. Code that looks a row or column up by its 1.0.x name must be changed, because an old name matches nothing and gives no error: x$value[x$term == "rho"] returns numeric(0). The columns of eta_squared(), omega_squared(), ci_eta_squared(), and ci_omega_squared() are under One Function for Each ANOVA Effect Size.

The limits of every confidence interval are ci_lower and ci_upper. DMAR 1.0.x named them lower_limit and upper_limit in most functions and ci_lower and ci_upper in the coefficient tables and the tidy() results. One pair is now used everywhere, as a row of a long table, a column of a wide one, and a suffix of a limit named for its estimate (rmsea_ci_lower, cles_ci_lower). x$value[x$term == "lower_limit"] becomes x$value[x$term == "ci_lower"], and x$lower_limit becomes x$ci_lower.

The reasons for each name are in One Notation for the Regression and Correlation Functions, below.

The removed rows suc_rep and num_probs_with_cis held counts of replications, which every sensitivity function now reports one way, in the simulation attribute of its table (see Changes to Earlier Results): suc_rep was the number of replications that gave an interval, and num_probs_with_cis the number that did not. reliability_H() returns the same table for every kind of input; the table of DMAR 1.0.0 is not returned for any call, and there is no warning period (see Coefficient H From a Fitted Model).

The column that holds a test statistic is test_statistic wherever the reference distribution depends on an option: under test = "t" in vargha_delaney_A(), and under a finite wald_df in the multilevel and confirmatory factor analysis tables, the statistic is referred to Student’s t, so z_value named it wrongly. The meta-analysis functions named their statistic t under hartung_knapp = TRUE and z without it (z in meta_contrast()); it is test_statistic in all four, with the reference distribution in the attributes test_distribution and test_df and in a line under the printed table, and the table of meta_contrast() now has the class dmar_meta_contrast, a dmar_tbl. Otherwise a column whose name is always true keeps it (z_value in cohen_kappa() and fleiss_kappa(), t_value in welch_t() and its relatives).

The common language effect size is the row cles wherever it is reported: cles() named it cl, as randomization_test() did not, and results_sentence() on a cles() table begins “cles =” where it began “cl =”.

ss_power_R2_change() is new in this release, so its rows true_f2 and true_partial_R2 have no 1.0.x names; they are named as planning values like every other row that holds one. The same holds for the other functions new in this release: ss_aipe_two_phase(), ss_aipe_two_phase_cost(), and ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity() echo true_cor, and the sensitivity function supposed_sd_Y and supposed_cor; equivalence_proportion_paired() reports its bounds in the rows prop_diff_lower and prop_diff_upper; ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity() echoes supposed_sd; ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity() echoes supposed_var_unit, supposed_var_rater, and supposed_var_residual; and ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity() echoes supposed_icc_X.

Calls That Are Now Refused

  • var_r() no longer takes kurtosis_x and kurtosis_y. DMAR 1.0.x returned a row var_r_bonett_wright, the normal-theory variance times 1 + rho^2 (kurtosis_x + kurtosis_y) / 4, and credited it to Bonett and Wright (2000). That article has no such formula, no other source for it was found, and the help’s statement that it is exact for elliptical distributions was wrong: there the variance is the normal-theory variance times one factor that does not depend on the correlation. The large-sample variance under non-normality depends on every fourth-order cumulant of the joint distribution (Duncan & Layard, 1973, Equation 1.1), which two marginal kurtoses do not supply. A call that gives either argument stops with “unused argument”.

  • desired_power must be strictly between 0 and 1 in every power planner. ss_power_R2() accepted 0 and 1 (and returned a sample size for a power of 1); ss_power_pcm() made no check. Every ss_power_* function now applies one rule and gives one refusal, of class dmar_desired_power_invalid, that carries the value given.

  • The unbiased standardized mean difference on one degree of freedom is refused. smd(unbiased = TRUE) with n_1 + n_2 = 3 and smd_c(unbiased = TRUE) with n_C = 2 returned 0, because the correction factor of Hedges (1981) is 0 at one degree of freedom whatever the data. They now stop with a refusal of class dmar_hedges_correction_undefined that says why and what to do (unbiased = FALSE, or more observations). On no degrees of freedom (smd_c() from summary statistics with n_C = 1, which returned Inf, or NaN when the means were equal; smd() with one standard deviation and n_1 + n_2 = 2) the refusal has the same class and states its own reason: the correction factor is not defined there, because there is no standard deviation.

  • desired_power is checked when a sample size is given too. A power planner that is given a sample size computes the power and does not use desired_power; a value outside (0, 1) given with it was accepted without a word (ss_power_r(true_cor = .3, specified_N = 60, desired_power = 1) returned a table) and is now refused with dmar_desired_power_invalid.

  • smd() from summary statistics refuses a group of one that has its own standard deviation. With s_1 and s_2, n_1 = 1 and n_2 = 2 returned a number and two groups of one returned NaN, where raw data with a group of one were already refused. Each size must be at least 2; the refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid.

  • conf_level, alpha_level, width, and assurance are checked on entry, one way. conf_level and alpha_level are each a single number strictly between 0 and 1; width is a single positive finite number; assurance is NULL or a single number strictly between 0 and

    1. A value that is not (a negative or zero width, a level of 0, 1, or -1, NA, a logical, a character string, a vector of two) reached the computation in many functions. Fifteen planners searched without end for a width of 0 or below (ss_aipe_sm(true_sm = 10, width = -1), ss_aipe_R2(true_R2 = .5, p = 5, width = -1)); others returned a number for it (ss_aipe_rmsea() 20,000, ss_aipe_reliability() Inf); ci_c() returned limits of Inf and -Inf for conf_level = -1; and ss_power_reg_coef() did not return for alpha_level = 0. Each is now refused at the first line of the function with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid (dmar_assurance_invalid for assurance) that names the argument, carries the value given, and says what to give. The check is at the head of the 166 functions in which a degenerate value was found to run or to stop with R’s own message; a function with a narrower range of its own (a width below 2 for a correlation, a level below .5 for an equivalence test, an assurance above .5) applies it after. An argument with no default is checked when it is given.

  • A number that is missing, empty, or not a number is refused by name. An argument that holds one number and was given as NA, NaN, a character string, a list, or a vector of length 0 stopped inside the computation with R’s message (“missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, “non-numeric argument to binary operator”, “argument is of length zero”), which names neither the argument nor the function. In 79 functions those arguments are now checked on entry: ci_smd(smd = .5, n_1 = NA, n_2 = 10) stops with “‘n_1’ must be a number that is not missing; NA was given”, class dmar_argument_invalid. No call that returned a result is affected.

  • The interval functions check conf_level before the tail areas are derived from it. ci_pvaf(), ci_snr(), ci_srsnr(), ci_eta_squared(), ci_omega_squared(), and ci_sc() refused conf_level = 1.2 with a message about alpha_lower, an argument the call did not give. The refusal now names conf_level. ss_aipe_R2(), ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity(), and plot_R2() gave an empty message for conf_level = NULL; they give the same refusal.

  • ci_c() refuses one tail area given without the other. ci_c(means = c(1, 0), s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(1, -1), n_per_group = c(20, 20), conf_level = NULL, alpha_upper = .025) (n in 1.0.0) stopped in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0 with R’s own message, “Non-numeric argument to mathematical function”, and with only alpha_lower given, “arguments imply differing number of rows: 3, 2”. It is now refused with class dmar_argument_invalid, arg c("alpha_lower", "alpha_upper"): “Only ‘alpha_upper’ was given. ‘alpha_lower’ and ‘alpha_upper’ go together: each is the tail area beyond one limit, so the interval needs both. Give both (for example alpha_lower = .025 and alpha_upper = .025, or 0 for a one-sided interval), or neither and a ‘conf_level’.”

  • ss_power_c() and ss_power_sc() refuse a contrast of 0 when a sample size is to be found. A population contrast of 0 is the null hypothesis; the power is alpha_level at every sample size. The two functions searched a million sample sizes and stopped with “Failed to converge within reasonable sample size.” They now stop at once with a refusal of class dmar_argument_invalid that says so. With a sample size given they return the power at 0, as before. The nine power planners that had that message for a search that reaches its limit (ss_power_c(), ss_power_sc(), ss_power_c_ancova(), ss_power_smd(), ss_power_one_way_anova(), ss_power_factorial_anova(), ss_power_rm_anova(), ss_power_split_plot_anova(), ss_power_mixed_effects()) now say what it means (the effect at the planning values is too small for the power asked for at any size up to 1,000,000) and what to check; the class is dmar_computation_failed, as before.

  • ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity() refuses supposed_R2 together with specified_N. It ran the simulation at the sample size planned from the supposed value and ignored specified_N (a call with specified_N = 6 reported total_N 34). The coefficient of variation, Cliff’s delta, and reliability siblings refused the pair already; all four refusals now have class dmar_argument_invalid.

  • ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity() asks for width when it plans. With supposed_std_contrast and no width the call stopped inside the planner with “argument is of length zero”; it now stops with a refusal of class dmar_argument_invalid that names width.

  • ss_aipe_reliability() checks its two counts of replications. G_initial and G (initial_iter and final_iter in 1.0.x) each must be a single whole number of at least 1; a fractional number, 0, a negative number, NA, or more than one value reached the search unchecked and is now an error of class dmar_count_invalid, as for every other G.

  • ss_power_mixed_effects() refuses a missing or inadmissible cluster_size, true_icc, or specified_n_clusters_per_arm by class. Each refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid, carries the name of the argument, and says what the value must be and why. A cluster size or a number of clusters that is not finite was not refused in 1.0.x.

  • An element of effects with a field the composite planners do not read is refused. Each element of effects in ss_power_composite_anova(), ss_power_composite_factorial_anova(), ss_power_composite_ancova(), ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova(), and ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het() is a list of factors, true_f or true_eta_squared_partial, and label (and type under heterogeneous slopes). A field under any other name, the f and partial_eta_squared of 1.0.x among them, or an element with no name, was not looked at: with the sizes read from true_means it was dropped without a word. It is now an error of class dmar_argument_invalid that names the effect and the field and gives the fields that are read.

  • ss_power_c_ancova() refuses an n_per_group that is not a single finite number of at least 2 by class (dmar_argument_invalid). A size below 2 was a plain error in 1.0.x, and a size that is not finite was not refused.

  • An argument a function does not have is an error in 20 more functions. See the paragraph on ... under Old Names That R Still Matches.

  • bifactor_indices() refuses a fit with one group factor. A general factor beside a single group factor is not a bifactor model with subscales: its indices divide the common variance between those two factors alone, every item belongs to the one subscale, and PUC is 0. DMAR 1.0.0 refused only a fit with no group factor and described a fit with one when every item was listed under that factor (some of them with loadings fixed at zero). Such a fit now stops with a message that names the group factor and says what to fit instead, as it does in fa_bifactor() and ci_bifactor_indices(), which are new in this release.

  • The six ss_aipe_crd_es_*() planners refuse a width asked for without the effect size. The width of the interval is read from data simulated at true_es. Without true_es the four planners that take or return a width stopped with a message that did not name the cause (ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_width() said that the width seemed impossible to reach with the number of clusters); they now stop at once with a refusal of class dmar_argument_invalid that says why the effect size is needed and what to give. In ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget() and ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget() the expected width is asked for by supplying G: with G and without true_es the call stopped with “arguments imply differing number of rows: 660, 0”, and with G and without pr_treat or true_icc it returned the table without the width and without a word. Both are now refused with the same class, in a message that names every population value that is missing and says that G = NULL returns the size the budget buys without a width. A true_es that is not a single finite number is refused the same way. With one covariate (n_covariates = 1) the same two functions had no default for true_R2_within and true_R2_between, where the four planners that take a width have 0, and did not use true_icc for a missing true_icc_covariate as the help says: a call with G and a covariate and without all three stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” or “arguments imply differing number of rows”. The two proportions now default to 0 in all six functions, a missing true_icc_covariate is true_icc, and a value of any of the three that is not a single number in range is refused with class dmar_argument_invalid, by name.

  • The twelve cluster randomized planners (ss_aipe_crd_*() and ss_aipe_crd_es_*()) check their sizes, proportions, and allocation on entry. n_covariates must be a whole number of 0 or more, cluster_size a whole number of at least 2 (the cluster size searches start at 2), n_clusters a whole number of at least 3 + n_covariates (the interval has n_clusters - 2 - n_covariates degrees of freedom), pr_treat strictly between 0 and 1, and true_R2_between and true_R2_within in [0, 1), as the two standardized budget planners already required of a covariate. Each refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid and names the argument as arg. DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0 planned with whatever they were given (the calls are written with the 1.1.0 names; 1.0.0 gave the same results under its own): ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8) returned 17.5 clusters with n_covariates = .5, 5 with true_R2_between = 1.1, and 19 with true_R2_within = -.5. Fractional sizes were planned for and are now refused: cluster_size = 20.5 gave 62 clusters at width = .5, and ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width(width = .5, n_clusters = 60.5, ...) a cluster size of 23; so is cluster_size = 1, which gave 249 clusters. n_clusters = 2 stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” (ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width()) or returned an expected width of NaN (ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget()), and pr_treat = 0 or 1 searched without end. A fixed number of clusters that leaves a condition without a cluster is refused, wherever a width is computed, with reason "arm_without_clusters" and the fewest clusters that would do (fewest): ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, n_clusters = 5, pr_treat = .1, ...) returned a cluster size of 200 with an expected width of Inf, since round(5 * .1) = 0 clusters are treated, and is refused with fewest = 6. ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget() makes the check only when G asks for the width, since without G it does not use pr_treat: with cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, G = 2, true_icc = .2, true_es = .5 the same design returned a cluster size of 200 with an expected width of NaN in DMAR 1.0.0 and stopped with class dmar_computation_failed after simulating it in the development versions, and without G it still returns 200.

  • Costs and budgets in the cluster randomized planners must be single finite numbers of 0 or more, and costs of 0 are refused where they decide the design. Costs that are both 0 are refused (reason "costs_all_zero") in the budget planners and the both planners, and individual_cost = 0 (reason "individual_cost_zero") where the costs choose the cluster size: ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(), ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget(), ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(), and their ss_aipe_crd_es_*() counterparts. Each class is dmar_argument_invalid, and each message says what to give. A search over designs that all cost the same has no end. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0 all six budget planners searched without end with both costs 0 (none returned within 4 seconds), among them ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 0); so did, with cluster_cost = 10 and individual_cost = 0, ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, n_clusters = 20, ...), ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget() with the same arguments, ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8, ...), and ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, true_es = .5, true_icc = .2, pr_treat = .5, G = 2, seed = 113, ...), which with a budget of 1000 stopped instead with “‘from’ must be a finite number”. With the same costs ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(width = .5, ...) returned a table of NA with a character value column, and ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_width() stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”. Clusters of a fixed size cost only their clusters, so ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget() with individual_cost = 0 and a positive cluster_cost still plans (100 clusters for a budget of 1000 at cluster_cost = 10). In the four planners that plan from a width and a fixed size the costs only price the plan, and costs of 0 still give a budget of 0. A negative cost, a vector of costs, and a negative budget were used, and are refused: ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = .5, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8, cluster_cost = -1, individual_cost = 1) reported a budget of 1178 (62 clusters at 19 each), ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 20, individual_cost = c(1, 2)) stopped with “arguments imply differing number of rows”, and ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = -5, cluster_size = 20) returned NA, in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions.

  • A budget that does not buy the smallest design a cluster randomized planner can return is refused with the cost of that design. The refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid, arg "budget", reason "budget_infeasible", and min_cost, and the budget it names buys a design the planner returns: ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1, cluster_size = 10, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1) (4 clusters of 10 cost 80) and ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 1, n_clusters = 10, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1) (10 clusters of 2 cost

    1. returned a table whose size and budget were NA in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0, as did their ss_aipe_crd_es_*() counterparts; ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget(budget = 1, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, ...) and ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_budget() with the same budget stopped with “invalid ‘type’ (list) of argument” (4 clusters of 2 cost 48). When the width is asked for (pr_treat, or G in the standardized planner), the smallest design ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget() can return has a cluster in each condition and a degree of freedom: ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 60, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .1, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8) returned a table of NA in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions, and is refused with the cost of 6 clusters, 120 (with n_covariates = 2 and pr_treat = .5, 5 clusters, 100); ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget() with the same budget and G = 2, true_icc = .2, true_es = .5 stopped with “NA/NaN argument” in both.

  • A budget that buys clusters of a fixed size with no finite width is refused when pr_treat asks for the width. ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 100, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .1, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8) returned 5 clusters, none of them treated, with an expected_width of Inf in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0. It is refused (class dmar_argument_invalid, reason "arm_without_clusters") with the budget, the design it buys, and the cheapest design that puts a cluster in each condition (6 clusters, cost 120); a design with no degrees of freedom (4 clusters with n_covariates = 2) is refused with reason "too_few_clusters". ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget() makes the same check before it simulates a width.

  • The six unstandardized cluster randomized planners refuse a negative, missing, or contradictory variance before searching. Any two of true_var_between, true_var_within, true_total_var, and true_icc determine the model. Each one given must be a single finite number (reason "variance_input_invalid"); a variance must be 0 or more, the total positive, whether it is given or is the sum of the two variances, and the intraclass correlation in [0, 1] (reason "variance_out_of_range"); fewer than two inputs, or a between variance of 0 with an intraclass correlation of 0, is refused with reason "underidentified_variances"; and a third or fourth input that disagrees with the two that determine the model by more than 64 machine epsilons of its scale is refused with reason "inconsistent_variances", with the value they imply in the message. With diff_size a within-cluster variance of 0 is refused (reason "within_variance_zero"), where the budget planners reported a width of NaN and the others stopped with an error from R. Each refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid, carries the four inputs as given in supplied, and says what to give. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0 ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = -.2, true_var_within = .8) stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” after ten warnings, as did true_total_var = 1, true_icc = NA without the warnings; true_var_between = 0, true_var_within = 0 returned 3 clusters with an expected width of 0; and true_total_var = 1, true_icc = .2, true_var_between = .5 planned 36 clusters with a between variance of .5 and a within variance of .8, where the pair (total 1, ICC .2) gives 18; it is now refused with “true_total_var = 1 and true_icc = 0.2 imply true_var_between = 0.2, but 0.5 was given”. A rounded redundant value is refused the same way: true_var_between = 1, true_var_within = 2, true_icc = .333, which DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions planned from the two variances (71 clusters), says that the variances imply true_icc = 0.333333333333333; give two of the four.

  • G above 999,999 is refused by the six ss_aipe_crd_es_*() planners. Each simulated data set takes its own seed, drawn without replacement from 1 to 999,999. ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 10, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, G = 1000000, pr_treat = .5, true_icc = .2, true_es = .5) stopped with “cannot take a sample larger than the population when ‘replace = FALSE’” in DMAR 1.0.0 (nrep) and the development versions of 1.1.0; it is refused on entry with class dmar_count_invalid, max 999999, and a message that says why. The draw of seeds is unchanged, so every G that was accepted gives the same seeds and the same result.

  • The cluster randomized planners check assurance, and the standardized ones width, conf_level, and the covariate’s intraclass correlation, on entry. ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width() and ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_width() check width, conf_level, and assurance as the other planners do: ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = -1, cluster_size = 20, true_es = .5, true_icc = .2, pr_treat = .5, G = 2) searched without end in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0. ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(), ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget(), and ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget() refuse an assurance that is not NULL or a single number strictly between 0 and 1 (class dmar_assurance_invalid), whether or not a width is computed, as the other planners do. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8, assurance = 1.5) returned 33 clusters with an assured width of NaN, and without the population values and with assurance = 2 33 clusters and a budget of 990; the two standardized planners with G = 2 and assurance = 2 stopped with “‘probs’ outside [0,1]”, and without G returned the size the budget buys (50 clusters of 10 at cluster_cost = 10). The four standardized planners that take a width or search over both sizes check true_icc_covariate (a single number in [0, 1]) on entry, as the two budget planners already did with G: ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, true_es = .5, true_icc = .2, pr_treat = .5, n_covariates = 1, true_icc_covariate = 1.5, true_R2_within = .1, true_R2_between = .1, G = 2, seed = 113) stopped with “‘data’ must be of a vector type, was ‘NULL’” in DMAR 1.0.0 and, after simulating three designs, with class dmar_computation_failed (reason "no_finite_width") in the development versions; it is refused with class dmar_argument_invalid and arg "true_icc_covariate".

  • The cluster randomized planners refuse a diff_size, true_icc, or es_type that makes the width not a number, and a target that no design of up to 1,000,000 clusters meets. diff_size must be NULL or a vector of one or more finite numbers, in all twelve planners. Wherever a width is simulated, the six ss_aipe_crd_es_*() planners check es_type (0, 1, or 2) and true_icc, a single number in [0, 1), and above 0 with es_type = 2: at 1 no variance lies within clusters and the model fitted to each simulated data set has none to estimate, and with es_type = 2 an intraclass correlation of 0 leaves the effect without a scale. Each refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0 ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, true_es = .5, true_icc = 1, pr_treat = .5, G = 2, seed = 113) stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, as it did with true_icc = 1.5, true_icc = -.2, and true_icc = 0, es_type = 2; with true_icc = 1, es_type = 0 it stopped with that message in 1.0.0, and the development versions simulated three designs at which every fit failed and stopped with class dmar_computation_failed. ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8) stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” with diff_size = numeric(0), c(Inf, 0), or NA, and with “non-numeric argument to mathematical function” with diff_size = "a". The searches over the number of clusters consider at most 1,000,000 clusters, the bound the power planners use for a sample size, and a target that no design within it meets is refused with arg "width", reason "n_clusters_beyond_reach", and the width at the bound as width_at_max: in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions the same call searched without end with width = 1e-300 and returned 1,639,025 clusters with width = .003, and ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(width = .003, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8) returned 1,391,996 clusters of 209. A target met within the bound is planned as before (width = .004: 921,953 clusters). The standardized planners start from this search and refuse such a target before anything is simulated. A width that is not a number at a design a search compares stops it with class dmar_computation_failed and reason "width_not_a_number"; the checks on entry leave no call that reaches it.

  • The twelve cluster randomized planners refuse a nonzero true_R2_between with n_covariates = 0. true_R2_between is the share of the between-cluster variance of the outcome that the cluster-level covariates explain, and n_covariates = 0 says there are none. Such a call is refused on entry, before any search or simulation, in all twelve planners, including the budget planners that compute no width. The refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid, arg "true_R2_between", and reason "R2_between_without_covariates", and its message asks for n_covariates or true_R2_between = 0. true_R2_within may still be nonzero without a cluster-level covariate. The plans these calls returned are under Changes to Earlier Results.

  • Summary statistics given with a fitted model are refused. Through 1.0.x eta_squared(fit, F_value = 3) and ci_eta_squared(fit, N = 50) ignored the summary statistics; eta_squared(), omega_squared(), ci_eta_squared(), and ci_omega_squared() now stop and say that a fitted model and summary statistics were both given. An infinite F_value is refused on entry by all four; ci_eta_squared() and ci_omega_squared() let it reach the noncentral root search, which failed.

  • ci_mahalanobis() refuses a name in ... that its root search does not take. tol, maxiter, check.conv, and trace are passed to the search of ci_nc_F(); any other name, and an argument with no name, is refused before anything is computed, with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid whose arg names it. DMAR 1.0.x passed every name on, so most stopped inside the search with a message about the search, and uniroot()’s lower, upper, f.lower, and f.upper replaced the bracket the search had set.

  • ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity() and ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity() refuse noncentral = TRUE when the sample size is planned from the supposed values and the supposed variances of Y and of the targeted predictor are not both 1, with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid whose message names ss_aipe_src_sensitivity(): the noncentral plan of ss_aipe_reg_coef() is for a standardized coefficient, and these two report the unstandardized one. With unit variances, or with specified_N, the call runs.

  • bifactor_indices() refuses a multiple-group fit, with the error average_variance_extracted() gives such a fit (class dmar_argument_invalid, the groups carried as groups): the factors have indices in each group, those of the model fitted to that group’s data alone. ci_bifactor_indices() already refused such a fit.

  • ss_aipe_cv() refuses a plan that cannot exist. With alpha_upper = 0 the interval is a lower confidence bound whose upper limit is infinite at every sample size; in DMAR 1.0.0 the search ran its cap of 100,000 steps (about a minute) before stopping with the error “The sample size search did not converge within 100000 iterations”. Such a call is now refused at once with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid naming alpha_upper. With alpha_lower = 0, an upper confidence bound, DMAR 1.0.0 returned no plan for any width: ci_cv() gave that interval a lower limit of -Inf, so its width was infinite at every sample size and the search stopped at the same cap. The lower limit is now 0, and the width is the upper bound itself. With alpha_upper below .5 the bound stays above true_cv at every sample size the search can reach, so a width at or below true_cv is refused the same way, naming width and alpha_lower. A wider target is planned without assurance (true_cv = .2, width = .25, conf_level = NULL, alpha_lower = 0, and alpha_upper = .05 give 37) and is refused with it (see the entry below on assurance together with alpha_lower = 0).

  • ss_aipe_sc() and ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity() take the contrast weights ci_sc() takes: weights that sum to zero and whose positive values sum to 1, with ci_sc()’s messages and class dmar_argument_invalid. ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(.25, .25, -.5), width = .4) returned 41 for a contrast ci_sc() refuses to estimate. Integer weights such as -1:1 are accepted, as before.

  • ss_aipe_sc_ancova() refuses unequal alpha_lower and alpha_upper (class dmar_argument_invalid, naming both). It plans for the interval of ci_sc_ancova(), which has equal tails only, and with unequal tails planned for an interval no DMAR function reports (alpha_lower = .01 and alpha_upper = .04 returned 215 at true_std_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(1, -1), and width = .4).

  • ss_aipe_sc_ancova(divisor = "s_anova") refuses a ratio of the ANCOVA to the ANOVA error standard deviation outside (0, 1], which no population has (class dmar_argument_invalid): true_cor = 1 stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, and true_sd_anova = 1 with true_sd_ancova = 2 returned 508 at true_contrast = 1 and width = .5.

  • Every function that takes contrast weights refuses weights that are all zero (class dmar_argument_invalid; arg is "c_weights", or the name the function gives the weights: "contrast" in contrast_adjusted(), "weights" in meta_contrast(), and "contrasts" in ci_scheffe(), contrast_test(), and is_orthogonal_set()). Such weights pass the rules that the weights sum to zero and that the positive ones sum to at most 1, and they define no contrast. The message is “‘c_weights’ has no nonzero weight, so it defines no contrast; give weights such as c(1, -1) or c(1/2, 1/2, -1).”, with the function’s own name for the weights in place of ‘c_weights’ (“‘contrast’ has no nonzero weight, …” in contrast_adjusted()). Where the weights are a set of contrasts (the rows of a matrix c_weights in ci_c_ancova_bp(), the rows of contrasts in contrast_test(), the columns of contrasts in ci_scheffe() and is_orthogonal_set()), a set with one such contrast is refused, and the message names it (“Row 2 of ‘c_weights’ has no nonzero weight”, “The contrast ‘none’ in ‘contrasts’ has no nonzero weight”). The functions are ci_c(), ci_c_ancova(), ci_c_ancova_bp(), ci_sc(), ci_sc_ancova(), ci_scheffe(), contrast_adjusted(), contrast_test(), equivalence_c(), is_orthogonal_set(), meta_contrast(), power_equivalence_c(), ss_aipe_c(), ss_aipe_c_ancova(), ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_c_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_sc(), ss_aipe_sc_ancova(), ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity(), ss_power_c(), ss_power_c_ancova(), ss_power_contrast(), ss_power_equivalence_c(), ss_power_sc(), ss_seq_c(), and ss_seq_c_sensitivity(). With c_weights = c(0, 0) (or three zeros where the design has three groups), DMAR 1.0.0:

    • returned the interval [0, 0] from ci_c(means = c(1, 2), s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(0, 0), n_per_group = c(20, 20)), from ci_c_ancova() with either procedure, from ci_c_ancova_bp(), and from contrast_adjusted(), ci_scheffe(), and contrast_test(), and [.5, .5] from ci_c(contrast = .5, s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(0, 0), n_per_group = c(20, 20)) and from ci_c_ancova() with contrast = .5; ci_scheffe() and contrast_test() reported a standard error of 0 beside the interval, and contrast_adjusted(), ci_scheffe(), and contrast_test() a test statistic and p-value of NaN;
    • returned a plan of 2 per group from ss_aipe_c(true_var_error = 1, c_weights = c(0, 0), width = .5), with or without assurance = .9, and from ss_aipe_c_ancova(), and a summary of zeros (every simulated contrast and width 0, pct_ci_less_width 1) from ss_aipe_c_sensitivity() and ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity();
    • returned 2 per group, a power of 1, and a noncentrality parameter of Inf from ss_power_c(true_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(0, 0), true_sd = 1), ss_power_c_ancova(), and ss_power_sc(), and a power of 1 with specified_n_per_group = 10;
    • reported all_orthogonal 1 from is_orthogonal_set(cbind(c(1, -1, 0), c(0, 0, 0)));
    • stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” in ss_aipe_sc(), ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_sc_ancova(), ci_sc_ancova(), and ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity() with supposed_std_contrast, and with “object ‘k’ not found” in ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity() with specified_n_per_group;
    • stopped with an unclassed message about the positive weights in ci_sc() (“Please use fractions to specify the contrast weights”), ss_power_contrast(), equivalence_c(), power_equivalence_c(), ss_power_equivalence_c(), ss_seq_c(), and ss_seq_c_sensitivity(), and with “All contrast weights are zero after centering.” in meta_contrast().

    Empty weights, c_weights = numeric(0), have no nonzero weight either, and they get the same refusal wherever no earlier check of their length refuses them. DMAR 1.0.0 returned the limits NaN around the contrast .5 from ci_c(contrast = .5, s_anova = 1, c_weights = numeric(0), n_per_group = 20) and from ci_c_ancova(contrast = .5, s_ancova = .8, c_weights = numeric(0), n_per_group = 20, cov_means = numeric(0), SSwithin_x = 40), the limits NaN around a contrast of 0 with means = numeric(0) or adj_means = numeric(0) in place of contrast, and [.5, .5] from ci_c() with N = 40 added. It stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” in ss_aipe_c(true_var_error = 1, c_weights = numeric(0), width = .5), ss_aipe_c_ancova(), ss_aipe_c_sensitivity(), ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity() (with empty true_mean_Y), ss_aipe_sc_ancova(), and ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity(), and a matrix that holds no contrast stopped with a message from R (“arguments imply differing number of rows: 1, 0” from ci_c_ancova_bp(adj_means = c(1, 2), s_ancova = .8, c_weights = matrix(numeric(0), 0, 2), n_per_group = 20), and “length of ‘dimnames’ [2] not equal to array extent” from ci_scheffe() with contrasts = matrix(numeric(0), 3, 0)), as did a set that holds no contrast in contrast_test() (“length of ‘dimnames’ [1] not equal to array extent” with contrasts = matrix(numeric(0), 0, 3), and “argument must be coercible to non-negative integer” with contrasts = list()). In the other functions DMAR 1.0.0 stopped on empty weights with a message about the length or form of the weights, the number of groups or contrasts, the positive weights, or the degrees of freedom; where a check of the length comes first (as in ss_power_c(), whose weights must have length 2 or more), DMAR 1.1.0 refuses them with that check’s message.

    Logical weights that are all FALSE, which are zeros when R computes with them, are refused too: with the message above, or, in the functions that require numeric weights, with that rule’s message. Those functions refused them with the same message in DMAR 1.0.0, without a class, except ci_sc(), ss_aipe_sc(), and ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity(), which require numeric weights from this release on: there DMAR 1.0.0 stopped with “Please use fractions to specify the contrast weights” (ci_sc()) and “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” (the two planners). DMAR 1.0.0 returned [0, 0] from ci_c(means = c(1, 2), s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(FALSE, FALSE), n_per_group = 20) and a plan of 2 per group from ss_aipe_c(true_var_error = 1, c_weights = c(FALSE, FALSE), width = .5).

    Weights in which every contrast has a nonzero value are accepted or refused as before, and the results for them are unchanged.

  • ss_aipe_sc() and ss_aipe_sc_ancova() refuse a width that needs more than 2^53 per group (about 9.0e15, the largest number up to which R holds every whole number exactly; class dmar_argument_invalid, naming width). Past it neighboring sample sizes can be the same number in R, so no size there is the smallest that reaches width. DMAR 1.0.0 returned such numbers at a standardized contrast of 0: ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = 0, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = 5e-8) (psi_standardized in 1.0.x) gave 12,292,668,226,221,188, and width = 1e-9 gave 30,731,670,565,552,979,968. Those calls are now refused, both when the start of the search is past 2^53 and when the search passes it (as at true_std_contrast = .1 with a start of 9,006,298,534,815,513 per group). Below the limit the plans are returned at every contrast: ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = 2, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = 1e-6) gives 46,097,505,846,480, and true_std_contrast = .1 with width = 5.9e-8 gives 8,839,438,422,537,546; DMAR 1.0.0 raised the sample size by one from a start about a third below the first and did not return either within 60 seconds. Past about 1e11 per group the plans rest on the precision of doubles (Details of ?ss_aipe_sc and ?ss_aipe_sc_ancova give the sizes). The smallest sample sizes here are for width and the tail areas as R holds them; with the default conf_level = .95 each tail area, (1 - .95) / 2, is 0.025000000000000022 in doubles. At a contrast of 0, where the width is computed from the normal quantiles, width = 6e-7 gives 85,365,751,570,981, the smallest sample size that reaches it, where DMAR 1.0.0 gave 85,365,751,570,976; width = 1e-6 gives 30,731,670,565,553, also the smallest, where DMAR 1.0.0 gave 30,731,670,565,548; and width = 1e-7 gives 3,073,167,056,555,298, 2 below the smallest, where DMAR 1.0.0 gave 3,073,167,056,555,294. At other contrasts the width is the difference of two limits near the noncentrality: the plan above at a contrast of 2 and width = 1e-6 is 1,850 below the smallest, 46,097,505,848,330 (see Bug Fixes for the search, and Changes to Earlier Results for the noncentral t distribution at many degrees of freedom).

  • ss_aipe_reg_coef(), ss_aipe_rc(), and ss_aipe_src() refuse a tail probability of 0 or above .5, and two tails of .5, with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid naming alpha_lower and alpha_upper. With a tail of 0 the interval has a limit at infinity and is never as narrow as width, and ci_reg_coef(), which reports the interval, takes no tail above .5.
